benchmarks.task_description:
fix: allow bootstrap and backup Jobs to reach managed database

The managed-database policy currently admits only server pods. Bootstrap and backup Jobs use different component labels, so their direct PostgreSQL connections are blocked when NetworkPolicy is enforced.

Add separate instance-scoped peers for bootstrap and backup pods to the existing TCP 5432 ingress rule. The policy still selects only this instance's database, admits peers only from its namespace, and denies database egress.

The regression test uses pod labels from the actual server, bootstrap Job and backup CronJob builders. It fails for both Jobs before the fix and passes afterward, including default/managed mode, with checks rejecting other instances, namespaces, components, ports and UDP.

Validation:
- Full non-E2E suite on Go 1.25.14 and `make test` on shipped Go 1.27.4, using cached Kubernetes 1.34.0 envtest assets.
- `make lint` with golangci-lint 2.15.0: zero issues.
- Independent source review and `git diff --check`.
- Hosted [CI](https://github.com/stubbi/paperclip-operator/actions/runs/44552389658) and all five [conformance jobs](https://github.com/stubbi/paperclip-operator/actions/runs/44552389693) passed on `04af89b`. The existing dependency findings in #135 remain separate.

Live CNI connectivity was not tested. This repairs the policy selectors; it does not resolve the separate authenticated-bootstrap, local-trusted bind, or dependency issues (#131, #132, #135).

Fixes #138.

fix(client): the Unique Status window reads its saved book when a character attaches, not at boot

## Summary

Since #4100 the client stops on the loading screen at every boot:

```
ReferenceError: Cannot access 'platform' before initialization
    at Object.uniqueNotifyBook (runtime.ts)
    at createUi (ui.ts)
    at startRuntime (runtime.ts)
```

`createUi` built the Unique Status window with `extensions.uniqueNotifyBook?.()`, which calls `platform.uniqueNotifyBook()` while `startRuntime` is still above its `const platform` (the platform is installed after every UI recipient exists, on purpose). The window now takes a getter and reads the book in `attach()`, when a character is chosen and the platform exists. A plain book object is still accepted (the existing tests use one).

The new grant `unique-status-hud.ts -> ui.ts callback:createUniqueStatusHud:0` is declared in `execution-contract.json`.

## Player note

None (the crash never reached a release).

## Old tab

Not affected (UI construction only, nothing a tab receives or decodes).

## Evidence

- [x] rg: blast radius pasted - `createUniqueStatusHud` has one product caller (`ui.ts`) and the test file; `uniqueNotifyBook` is read only there.
- [x] callers: every caller and test of each changed function mapped - `ui.ts` passes the getter; the 6 existing tests keep passing a plain book.
- [x] edge cases: mapped, each with a test or a reason - new test: the getter is not read at construction (it throws if it is) and is read once on attach.
- [ ] native client: n/a - no native claim
- [ ] native server: n/a - no native claim
- [x] subs: no unlabelled subs left in what was read

## Native claims

none

## Verification

- `node tools/run-tests.mjs tests/runtime/unique-status.test.mjs` - exit 0 (20 tests)
- `pnpm --filter @sro/client-next verify:quick` - exit 0
- `pnpm verify:test-types` - exit 0 (no new errors)
- `pnpm exec dprint check` on the changed files - exit 0
- Manual: local `pnpm local` on main aba562eb5 stopped on the loading screen with the error above; with the fix the client reaches login and character select with no console errors.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(sync): remove Epic session directories left behind by a crash

If the server crashes during an Epic sign-in or sync, that operation's `session-*` directory (added in #1384) stays in `LEGENDARY_WORK_DIR` with the user's Legendary credentials in it, and nothing removed it.

Startup now deletes `session-*` directories older than an hour.

- **Age limit:** an hour is well beyond the longest sign-in or sync. It keeps the sweep from deleting an operation still running on another server if several share the directory.
- **Scope:** only `session-*` directories are touched. Files and other directories, such as the legacy per-user ones, are left alone.
- **Failures:** if the directory is unset or missing, the sweep does nothing. A directory that can't be removed is logged and skipped, so startup never fails on it.

It runs at startup only. A crashed operation always means a restart, so a periodic job would add nothing.

Tests cover:

- an old session is removed
- a recent session is kept
- legacy directories and `session-*` files are untouched
- an unset or missing work directory is left as it is

Closes #1387

benchmarks.task_description: fix(metadata): label Sportarr episodes by their local broadcast date ## Problem Related issue: https://github.com/Silo-Server/silo-server/discussions/5046 Silo shows Sportarr events by their synthetic season and episode numbers, so an NBA game reads "S2026E296". Silo-Server/silo-server#5129 lets a metadata plugin ask for a series' episodes to be labeled by date instead, but this plugin doesn't ask yet. The date it sends is also a day late for many games: it uses Sportarr's `air_date`, the UTC date of the start, so a 7:30 PM game in New York on Nov 20 is dated Nov 21. ## Approach - Episodes now take their air date from Sportarr's `broadcast_date`, the local day of the event, and fall back to `air_date` only when `broadcast_date` is missing. - Series results set `metadata.episode_labels = "air_date"`, so a server with Silo-Server/silo-server#5129 labels the league's episodes by date. Older servers ignore the field. - The README explains both. The manifest version stays 1.0.5; the release bump is left to a maintainer. ## Validation - `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `gofmt -l .` with `GOWORK=off`: pass, including new tests for the date fallback and the series flag. - End to end: a local Silo server with Silo-Server/silo-server#5129 and this plugin, against a Sportarr instance with NBA, NHL, MLB, NFL, Formula 1 and UFC leagues. After a metadata refresh, evening games carry the local date and the web, Apple and Android clients show it. - Maintainer review: the new series-flag test fails on the base. Live Sportarr data confirms `broadcast_date` follows each league's broadcast time zone, which is also the date Sportarr's renamer writes into file names. The comments and README now say so. ## Evidence Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-plugin-metadata-sportarr/pr-12/ The plugin has no UI, so that page holds the test and API results. The visible result is in the evidence for Silo-Server/silo-server#5129, Silo-Server/silo-apple#1252 and Silo-Server/silo-android#1035, captured with this plugin. ## Risks - Existing episodes keep their stored dates until their league's metadata next refreshes; **Refresh All Metadata** on the library applies the new dates at once. Dates an admin locked stay as they are. - Libraries matched from NFO files never call this plugin, so they keep their numbers. ## Checklist - [x] I read and can explain the complete diff. - [x] This pull request addresses one concern. ## AI Disclosure - Harness: Claude Code (in T3 Code) - Tool(s): Claude Code; Codex CLI for the second reviewer - Model(s): claude-opus-5-5; gpt-6.2-sol (review) - Involvement: Fully AI-generated, human verified - Adversarial review: dual code review (claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-6.2-sol, independent, then reconciled) of this branch together with the server and client changes; no open findings. > [!NOTE] > ### Use `broadcast_date` as the episode air date for Sportarr series > - Sportarr episodes have a `broadcast_date` (local broadcast) distinct from `air_date`. New `episodeAirDate` in [provider.go](https://github.com/Silo-Server/silo-plugin-metadata-sportarr/pull/12/files#diff-0e3b5cd2e6abf4633712dbd2d69307b7fbd75bc71844e34306afdcd9840dab64) returns `BroadcastDate` when set, else `AirDate`, and `Provider.GetEpisodes` uses it for the episode `AirDate`. > - Adds `BroadcastDate` field (JSON `broadcast_date`) to `AgentEpisode` in [types.go](https://github.com/Silo-Server/silo-plugin-metadata-sportarr/pull/12/files#diff-617c35037dd46f087b7be4c7ce57c90adc394741004cc65d988f4bfdc05b9d42), so the date is decoded from the agent response. > - `metadataItemFromResult` in [main.go](https://github.com/Silo-Server/silo-plugin-metadata-sportarr/pull/12/files#diff-2873f79a86c0d8b3335cd7731b0ecf7dd4301eb19a82ef7a1cba7589b5252261) now sets `metadata.episode_labels` to `air_date` for series items, with a matching test. > - Risk: episodes without a `broadcast_date` keep the old `air_date` behavior; episodes with both now use `broadcast_date`, changing `GetEpisodes` output where the two dates differ. > > > > Macroscope summarized 2d2bdb0. > >

diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
index 2ad0b52..2430db3 100644
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -2,6 +2,20 @@
 
 First-party Silo metadata plugin backed by [Sportarr](https://sportarr.net). Provides sports league metadata as TV shows, with series, seasons, and episodes mapped from leagues, seasons, and events.
 
+## Episode Dates and Labels
+
+Sportarr numbers a league's events `S<year>E<n>` so they sort like a TV season.
+Those numbers mean nothing to viewers, so series returned by this plugin carry
+`metadata.episode_labels = "air_date"`, which asks Silo to label their episodes
+by date instead.
+
+An episode's air date is Sportarr's `broadcast_date`: the day of the event in
+its broadcast time zone, which is also the date Sportarr writes into file names.
+The plugin falls back to `air_date`, the UTC date of the start, only when
+`broadcast_date` is missing. `air_date` can be a day off: an evening game in the
+Americas lands on the next day, and an afternoon event in Australia on the day
+before.
+
 ## Dependency Model
 
 This repository consumes `github.com/Silo-Server/silo-plugin-sdk` as a normal Go module dependency. CI and release builds run with `GOWORK=off` and expect the SDK version in `go.mod` to resolve from a published semver tag.

When the hero came back into view, the timer started a fresh cycle while the rail was already full, so the rail sat full for about 8 seconds before the slide changed. Now the rail stops with the timer and starts again from empty when the timer restarts. ## Approach `HeroBanner` already restarts the rail animation by remounting it whenever the slideshow starts running again (a hold ends or Play is pressed). That logic only looked at the Pause choice and the hover and focus holds, not at whether the hero is shown. fix(client): a Magic Pop voucher shows no invented magic stats

﻿Classification: bug - the port's client invented magic-attribute lines on the Magic Pop result voucher; the retail client prints the same bogus line (see the native-claims table); hiding it is a port-only display-defect fix, shipped as the default per the owner's 2026-11-21 rule. Fixed client-side; no behaviour change beyond the tooltip lines.

Fixes #4151

## What the ticket is

The item named "Item Exchange Ticket" is `ITEM_MALL_GACHA_CARD_WIN` (its lose twin `ITEM_MALL_GACHA_CARD_LOSE` shares the name and the shape): the Magic Pop result card, TID 3.3.14.2. It carries its prize as two indexed item params - reward RefObjID, then quantity - which the exchange operator reads back. It is not rolled magic options, and the roll that creates the card writes no options; the params only ever *looked* like options to the tooltip.

## The bug

`itemTooltipMagic` walked the item's encoded option words and looked each low word up as a magicoption param id. For the voucher, word two is the prize quantity, and any quantity in 1..255 collides with a real magicoption row (id 1 is `MATTR_DEC_MAXDUR`), so the tooltip printed a bogus attribute line - the reported blue stats. The fix gates the voucher type out of the option walk, reusing the existing `isGachaVoucher` predicate. The pair stays on the item (the exchange reader consumes it), and the item name keeps its blue colour, which is what the native client does (below).

## Native claims

| Claim | Evidence | How checked | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The voucher's two params are stored keyed by index 0/1, not by magicoption id | Client `CSOItem_DeserializeMagicOptions` 0x0078B1B0: under the `CItemData_IsGachaCard_Tid3_14_Tid4_2` 0x00550870 branch it inserts only indices 0 and 1 into the map at item+0xA4 (`CSOItem_GetMagicOptionMap` 0x00789330) with the u64 low dwords as values | revtool/rizin disassembly of the v1.150 client; labelled in the client symbol ledger | Confirmed |
| No magic line can format for the pair | **Refuted (rebuild-ab-claude, read at 317061003):** the walk `CIFItemTooltip_AppendMagicOptionRows` 0x563700 looks each key up with 0x7E10C0 at 0x5639F9 and formats it through 0x55B540 at 0x563A6F with no null check, so key 1 reads as MATTR_DEC_MAXDUR and retail prints a bogus line | rizin disassembly of 0x563700..0x563A8E | Refuted: the fix is port-only, a display-defect fix shipped as the default (owner 2026-11-21) |
| The voucher's blue item name is native and stays | `ItemTooltip_FormatNameWithPlus` 0x00564230 colours the name 0xFF72BFFF when `CSOItem_GetFlag84` 0x00789310 (the param count byte at +0x84) is nonzero; the voucher's count is 2 | revtool/rizin disassembly | Confirmed - deliberately unchanged |
| The server already writes the pair natively | The roll's row and 0x3645 delta carry the pair under the same type predicate (server `UsesIndexedMagicParams`, "they are not magicoption.txt reinforce rows") | Code read; no server change in this PR | Confirmed |

## Media

The issue has no attachment or comments (the in-game report path was broken when it was filed), so the screenshot done-when is unsatisfiable; the ticket was identified from the shipped name table instead (`SN_ITEM_MALL_GACHA_CARD_WIN` = "Item Exchange Ticket").

## What ran

- `tests/runtime/item-tooltip-magic.test.mjs`: 8 pass, including the new voucher case (mutation-checked: it fails with the gate disabled). Related suites `item-magic-definitions`, `gacha-window`, `tooltip-coverage`, `bag-tab-row`: all pass.
- `pnpm --filter @sro/client-next verify:quick`: PASS. `verify-test-types`: PASS (no new errors).
- `pnpm check source`: PASSED, 19 tasks. `check:format`: no new unformatted files.

Player-note: UI: The Magic Pop exchange ticket no longer shows invented magic stats in its tooltip.

Old-tab: safe - one tooltip branch gated by item type; every other item renders as before.
